title: Fix logout Unauthorized error and harden notifications within supported web capabilities

requirements.text: Fix the post-logout “Unauthorized User” bug by making the logout flow immediately transition the UI to the Login screen, cancel/stop any in-flight backend calls, and prevent any subsequent backend calls from being initiated after logout completes.

quotes: After logout, app shows “Unauthorized User” error.
Prevent any API call after logout

acceptanceCriteria: Tapping Settings → Log Out (and confirming) immediately returns the user to the Login screen (i.e., the login gate is reached) without showing any “Unauthorized” error UI.
Any in-flight React Query requests are cancelled/ignored during logout so they cannot surface errors after logout completes.
After logout completes, the app does not attempt background profile sync calls (e.g., saveCallerUserProfile) until the user logs in again.
The logout flow works consistently across repeated logout/login cycles in a single browser session without requiring a hard refresh.

requirements.text: Implement consistent, user-friendly handling for authorization-related backend errors so the app never shows raw “Unauthorized” text to users: map authorization failures to clean UX and recovery actions.

quotes:
Add proper error handling:

401 → logout and show session expired message

403 → show permission denied

acceptanceCriteria: If the frontend encounters a backend authorization failure (e.g., error text containing "Unauthorized" from canister traps), the app shows English messaging: "Your session expired. Please log in again." and transitions to the Login screen after clearing local session/app state.
If the frontend encounters a backend permission/forbidden-style failure (where identifiable), the app shows English messaging: "Permission denied." and does not crash.

The global ErrorBoundary fallback screen does not display raw backend authorization errors; it either (a) guides the user to reload, or (b) shows a session-expired style message with a clear recovery action.
No screen in the app renders the literal strings "Unauthorized" / "Unauthorized User" to the user as an unhandled error.

requirements.text: Harden the SettingsPage logout implementation to be resilient and ordered correctly: always clear device data (IndexedDB + ranking cache) and Internet Identity session without leaving the app in a partially logged-out state.

quotes:
Properly clear:

Local storage/session storage

Cached user data

On logout:

Invalidate token on backend (blacklist if needed)

Redirect to login screen immediately

acceptanceCriteria: On logout confirmation, the app clears: IndexedDB app state (via clearIndexedDB), rank cache (via clearRankingCache), and resets in-memory app state (dispatch RESET_ALL).
After logout, the Internet Identity session is cleared (existing clearIdentity call), and subsequent backend calls use anonymous identity until re-login.

If backend deletion (deleteCallerUser) fails, the app shows a clear English error and still provides a safe way to complete local logout (device data clearing + returning to Login) without leaving the user stuck on Settings.
No leftover per-session data used by the app (including any URL param–persisted secrets stored in sessionStorage by urlParams helpers) causes the UI to re-trigger authenticated flows after logout.

requirements.text: Upgrade the in-app notification settings UX to support separate notification preference categories (ranking alerts, reward alerts, streak reminders, etc.) within the existing supported web notification system, and persist these preferences via existing IndexedDB + backup/restore flows.

quotes:
Create notification settings:
For App Users:
Enable/Disable Push
Ranking updates
Reward alerts
Streak reminder
...
Store preferences in database: notificationSettings:

pushEnabled

rankingAlert

rewardAlert

streakReminder

withdrawalAlert

Before sending notification:
Check user settings first.

acceptanceCriteria: Settings → Notifications displays separate toggles (English labels) for at minimum: Enable Notifications, Ranking alerts, Reward alerts, Streak reminders (additional categories may be shown but must be clear and not misleading).

These notification preferences are persisted in the existing local persistence layer (IndexedDB) and included in export/import backup/restore without breaking older stored data (missing fields default safely).
Any in-app notification triggered by app events respects the new category toggles (e.g., if rankingAlert is off, ranking-related notifications are not shown).
All user-facing copy clarifies the actual supported behavior for this web build (i.e., browser notifications, not guaranteed when the app is closed).

requirements.text: Improve reliability and clarity of the existing “Send Test Notification” action to ensure it consistently provides visible feedback for all states (supported/unsupported, enabled/disabled, permission granted/denied) without silent failure.

quotes: FIX PUSH NOTIFICATION (NOT WORKING IN APK)
Debug and fix ... "Send Test Notification" ... reliably results in a visible browser notification ... provide clear in-app feedback when ... cannot be sent

acceptanceCriteria: When Notifications are supported, permission is granted, and notifications are enabled, pressing “Send Test Notification” produces a visible system notification.
When notifications cannot be sent, the UI shows an English reason-specific message (unsupported browser, permission denied, permission not granted yet, notifications disabled).
The test notification flow never throws an unhandled exception and never triggers the global ErrorBoundary.

requirements.text: Document and enforce platform limitations in Settings → Notifications so users are not misled: explicitly state that this build supports browser notifications while the app is running and does not provide true background push delivery when the app is closed.

quotes: Use English for any user-facing text

Ensure:
✅ Notifications work in APK
✅ Notifications work on Web
✅ Real-time delivery

acceptanceCriteria: Settings → Notifications includes clear English text stating: notifications require browser permission; delivery is not guaranteed when the app/browser is closed; behavior depends on browser support.
No UI text claims Firebase/FCM/APK push support unless it is actually implemented (and on this platform it must not be claimed).

constraints: Upgrade the existing BunkPro app; do not rebuild from scratch.

Frontend files under immutable paths must not be edited: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, and frontend/src/components/ui/* must remain unchanged.
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo; add backend changes only within that file unless a state migration is strictly necessary.

This platform does not support Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) integration, Android APK native configuration (google-services.json, AndroidManifest.xml), iOS push setup, JWT/refresh-token auth stacks, or service-worker-based FCM push. Notification improvements must be limited to supported web capabilities (browser Notifications API and in-app/local notifications while the web app is running).
Use English for all user-facing text.
nonGoals: Implementing FCM token registration/storage, Firebase projects, or sending true cross-platform push notifications to Android/iOS.
Adding or managing JWT/refresh tokens, token blacklists, or token-validation middleware typical of REST backends (the app uses Internet Identity + canister calls).
Building or modifying native Android/iOS project files (AndroidManifest.xml, notification channels, icons) or producing an APK/iOS app package.
Adding real-time push delivery when the web app is closed (not supported without external push infrastructure).
